checks.message: Event bus not encrypted with a customer managed KMS key
checks.context: Default encryption uses an AWS-owned key with no audit trail. A CMK gives you CloudTrail logs on every encrypt/decrypt and lets you revoke access instantly by disabling the key.

checks.message: Verify the event pattern is as specific as possible
checks.context: Overly broad event patterns (e.g. matching all EC2 events) can trigger rules on unintended events and create noisy or dangerous automation. Scope patterns to the exact source, detail-type, and fields you need.

checks.message: Verify the target has a scoped IAM role — not a wildcard trust policy
checks.context: EventBridge assumes the role you specify to invoke the target. If that role has broad permissions (e.g. lambda:* or ecs:*), a misconfigured rule can trigger unintended actions at scale.

checks.message: Deleting a rule stops all event-driven automation tied to it
checks.context: If this rule drives critical workflows (auto-remediation, notifications, pipeline triggers), deleting it silently breaks those flows. Disable the rule first and monitor for impact before deleting.

checks.message: Event archive inherits encryption from the source event bus
checks.context: Archives can contain sensitive event payloads. Encryption is inherited from the event bus — there is no separate KMS key parameter for archives. Ensure the source event bus has CMK encryption configured before creating an archive.

checks.message: Verify the schedule's execution role is scoped to only what the target needs
checks.context: EventBridge Scheduler assumes the role you provide to invoke the target. A broad role here means a misconfigured schedule can trigger destructive actions (e.g. deleting resources, invoking wrong Lambda) on a timer.

checks.message: Verify you are not granting PutEvents access to untrusted accounts or organizations
checks.context: EventBridge resource policies control who can put events on your event bus. A policy granting access to * or a broad organization allows any account to inject events that trigger your rules.

checks.message: Removing a permission may break cross-account event delivery
checks.context: If partner accounts or other AWS accounts send events to this bus, removing their permission immediately stops event delivery. Verify no active integrations depend on this permission.
